analysis:
Examined the docs update in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 2172-2184), the auto-paged policy addition in EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift (head lines 38-41), the new maskCacheKey and allowsChainedDecode in FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift, and the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump. No concrete security regression identified.

The policy change adds the exact string "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged list. It only picks a KV backend by exact model ID. It does not touch the coordinator wire contract, attestation, keys or authorization. Explicit contiguous selection, the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV kill switch, slot vetoes and the crash-loop guard still apply.

In FlintAnswerStopConstraint, maskCacheKey returns -1 for matched nodes and the base key for scanning nodes, and returns nil when the key is negative. This relies on the base maskCacheKey being state-pure. A key collision could in principle apply the wrong token mask, which would affect output-constraint correctness. That is a correctness and availability concern within the provider, not a confidentiality break. It also depends on the base FlintNativeProtocolConstraint implementation, which is not in the supplied units. allowsChainedDecode delegates to the base. Shared state is guarded by the lock, and the lock is released before calling into the base, so there is no new deadlock.

The constrained chaining that the docs describe (sampling step N+1 while step N is on the GPU, with redraw) lives in the mlx-swift-lm SDK. The submodule bump (889fe3c to 0349802) has no visible diff, so those engine changes are unreviewed. The open questions are whether chained decode preserves the constraint guarantees, i.e. the tool/reasoning boundary and the EOS masking; whether it affects the cancellation/lease behavior in T-010; and whether the residual KV or logits retention affects T-028. The prefix-cache (T-041) and SSD encryption paths are not changed by the supplied files.

Set needs_deeper_review=true because the submodule content is not visible.
